In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the DNA synthesis is a normal process in submandibular glands of the mouse.
DNA is present in all the cells of the gland and that the majority of the cells are involved in DNA synthesis.
the submandibular salivary gland is a useful experimental tool in the study of cell cycle kinetics.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the DNA content of the secretory cells is not constant during their maturation.
the submandibular glands of mice are not a suitable system for studying the relationship between the cell cycle and the secretory process.
the DNA synthesis is a dynamic process, which is regulated by a complex system of factors, which are responsible for the initiation of the process and for its duration.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have developed a new, non-invasive method to measure the amount of DNA in a single cell.
the use of collagenase/hyaluronidase for cell dissociation of the submandibular glands of mice is a reliable and simple method that can be applied to a wide range of experimental designs.
